accepted.title: A strongly polynomial algorithm for general linear programming
accepted.text: Does there exist an algorithm that, given A∈ℝ^{m×n}, b∈ℝᵐ and c∈ℝⁿ, solves min{cᵀx:Ax=b,x≥0}, or reports infeasibility or an unbounded objective, with a number of basic real-arithmetic operations and comparisons bounded by a polynomial in m,n independent of the coefficients? Use the source computational model, permitting +,−,×,÷, comparisons and square roots; for rational input the implementation must also use space polynomial in the input encoding length.

accepted.title: Integral conformal circuit decompositions with lcm denominator
accepted.text: Let W⊂ℝⁿ be a rational linear subspace. An elementary vector is a nonzero g∈W whose support contains no proper support of another nonzero vector in W. For each elementary support choose its primitive integer representative g, with gcd of its nonzero coordinates1, and let κ̇_W be the least common multiple of the absolute values of all their nonzero coordinates (κ̇_W=1 for the trivial cases). For every z∈W∩ℤⁿ, must there be h≤n elementary vectors g¹,…,gʰ with z=Σ_i gⁱ, κ̇_W gⁱ∈ℤⁿ, and z_jgⁱ_j>0 whenever gⁱ_j≠0? For z=0 the empty decomposition is allowed.
accepted.subject: Theory of Computation
accepted.scope_review: Physical20 conformality and physical22 Definition3.1.1 establish the lcm measure, not max or fractional imbalance. Integer vectors summing to z require coordinate denominator dividingκ̇_W; existing real conformal decompositions and anchored/prime-power cases are only partial results.
accepted.literature_finding: The held source’s general conjecture follows its special-case propositions and is still present in the current primary thesis copy. The2026 circuit-diameter theorem imposes no corresponding integer-denominator conclusion; no full resolution of this integral decomposition target was located.
